output.brief:
Don't roll back the gateway. The latency jump came from the storage compaction tuning pushed the evening of 2 Nov, not from gateway 5.8. In every cell that got the tuning, GET p99 jumped within minutes of the push, regardless of when 5.8 arrived. The one cell that skipped the tuning (aps-3) got 5.8 but stayed at about 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. After the tuning, storage disks went from 41% to 97% busy, and read-queue waits rose from 9 ms to 205 ms. Network and traffic growth don't explain it. A rollback would also reopen the signature vulnerability and miss the 30 Nov audit deadline.

Next steps: revert the compaction tuning in one cell first, watch p99 and compaction backlog, then extend to the rest. Backlog was 11.2% on 2 Nov, and the 15% danger line is not projected before 13 Nov, so there is time to do this carefully. Don't pause compaction fleet-wide. Hold off on throttling Orrin until the 10 Nov attribution report shows what drove the backlog. Confidence is high, about 85–90%. The main remaining unknown is what caused the backlog growth.
